newsitem.title: ITALY: Generali sees '97 premiums at 40 trln lire.
newsitem.headline: Generali sees '97 premiums at 40 trln lire.

text.p: Italian insurance giant Assicurazioni Generali SpA on Wednesday forecast the group's premium income in 1997 would rise to 40 trillion lire from 34.9 trillion lire in 1996 with the increase coming largely from life premiums.

The projections were given by the group's managing director Gianfranco Gutty at a meeting with analysts. He said life premium income was set to rise around 15 percent in 1997 while non-life premiums would be largely steady.
Gutty added that the company would use its excess cash, which amounted to 4.490 trillion lire, to make acquisitions in countries where the group did not have critical mass.

As regards France, where Generali has a market share of 3.2 percent, he confirmed the group's interest in French insurer Athena. But on the long-running rumour that Generali may takeover Italian insurer SAI, he said, "A good company but one that does not enter into our strategy".
